objective: Test structurally different breakout, recovery, acceleration, and defensive-event concepts independently before any parameter refinement or strategy combination.
research_basis: Long-horizon trend and time-series momentum have shown persistence across markets, but implementation and costs require out-of-sample validation.
Momentum can crash following market declines in high-volatility rebound states, motivating separate recovery and deterioration experiments.
Volatility scaling does not consistently improve every implementable strategy, so volatility contraction is treated as a standalone hypothesis rather than assumed beneficial.

candidates.concept: A sector emerging through a recent 20-session closing high while its short-term volatility is materially below its medium-term volatility may begin an expansion phase.
candidates.fixed_rules: 200-session positive trend; 20-session volatility no greater than 60 percent of 60-session volatility; breakout observed within five sessions; remain above 10-session mean; hold strongest sector.

candidates.concept: A longer closing-range breakout aligned with the prevailing trend may persist beyond a one-day new high.
candidates.fixed_rules: 200-session positive trend; 55-session closing breakout within ten sessions; remain above 20-session mean; hold strongest sector.

candidates.concept: A meaningful increase in short-horizon sector momentum may identify emerging leadership before a long-horizon rank fully adjusts.
candidates.fixed_rules: 20-session return exceeds its preceding 20-session return by at least three percentage points; positive 63-session return and 200-session trend; equal-weight top three.

candidates.concept: A rapid expansion from narrow to broad sector participation with a confirmed positive market trend may identify a durable recovery.
candidates.fixed_rules: Sector breadth rises from at most 35 percent during the prior five-to-ten sessions to at least 65 percent; SPY above its 20-session mean.

candidates.concept: A sharp pullback followed by an upward reversal may rebound differently when the long-term market trend remains positive.
candidates.fixed_rules: At least five-percent five-session SPY decline observed within five sessions; current close reverses upward; SPY remains above its 200-session mean.

candidates.concept: A rapid collapse in sector participation may favor temporarily rotating from SPY into a positively trending defensive asset.
candidates.fixed_rules: Breadth falls from at least 65 percent to at most 35 percent in five sessions; select the strongest positive 20-session return among BIL, IEF, and GLD, otherwise SHY; hold SPY when inactive.
